# laravel_cloud_database_restore (Resource)

Restores a Laravel Cloud database cluster from a snapshot or point-in-time, into a new cluster. The API gives a restored Serverless Postgres cluster the same ID as its source, so every request for it reaches the source: destroying such a restore only removes it from state, and the restored cluster has to be deleted in the Laravel Cloud dashboard.

~> **Beta:** This provider is in beta and may change between releases.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "laravel_cloud_database_cluster" "example" {
  name    = "my-app-db"
  type    = "laravel_mysql"
  version = "8.4"
  region  = "us-east-2"

  # The settings of the database type, as JSON. size is one of the sizes the
  # laravel_cloud_database_types data source lists for the type.
  config = jsonencode({
    size                     = "mysql-flex-1gb"
    storage                  = 10 # GiB
    is_public                = false
    uses_scheduled_snapshots = true
    retention_days           = 7
  })
}

resource "laravel_cloud_database_snapshot" "before_migration" {
  cluster_id = laravel_cloud_database_cluster.example.id
  name       = "before-2026-11-migration"
}

# Restores the snapshot into a new cluster; the source cluster is unchanged.
resource "laravel_cloud_database_restore" "from_snapshot" {
  database_cluster_id  = laravel_cloud_database_cluster.example.id
  name                 = "my-app-db-restored"
  database_snapshot_id = laravel_cloud_database_snapshot.before_migration.id

  # The restored cluster holds copies of the source cluster's databases.
  force_destroy = true
}

# Or restore the cluster as it was at a point in time:
#
# resource "laravel_cloud_database_restore" "point_in_time" {
#   database_cluster_id = laravel_cloud_database_cluster.example.id
#   name                = "my-app-db-pitr"
#   restore_time        = "2026-11-20T09:30:00Z"
# }
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `database_cluster_id` (String) Source database cluster ID to restore from.
- `name` (String) Name for the restored database cluster.

### Optional

- `database_snapshot_id` (String) Snapshot ID to restore from. Mutually exclusive with restore_time.
- `force_destroy` (Boolean) Allow destroying the restored cluster even though it still contains databases. A restore copies the source cluster's databases into the new cluster, and the API refuses to delete a cluster while any database is attached, so destroying is usually impossible without this. Setting it true DELETES EVERY DATABASE IN THE RESTORED CLUSTER, including ones Terraform does not manage. Defaults to false, in which case destroy fails and names the databases that are in the way.
- `restore_time` (String) Point-in-time to restore to (ISO 8601). Mutually exclusive with database_snapshot_id.

### Read-Only

- `config` (String) JSON-encoded configuration of the restored cluster.
- `connection_details` (Attributes) Read-only connection details for the restored cluster. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--connection_details))
- `id` (String) ID of the restored database cluster.
- `region` (String) Region of the restored cluster.
- `restored_cluster_name` (String) Name of the restored cluster.
- `restored_cluster_status` (String) Status of the restored cluster.
- `restored_cluster_type` (String) Type of the restored cluster.
